title: The ring of rational functions of a scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. If $U,V\subseteq X$ are dense open subsets, so is $U\cap V$. A *rational function* on $X$ is an equivalence class of pairs $(U,f)$ with $U\subseteq X$ a dense open subset and $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, where $(U,f)\sim(V,g)$ if $f|_W=g|_W$ for some dense open $W\subseteq U\cap V$ (this is an equivalence relation: for transitivity intersect the two dense opens). The *ring of rational functions* $R(X)$ is the set of rational functions with $[(U,f)]+[(V,g)]=[(U\cap V,f|_{U\cap V}+g|_{U\cap V})]$ and $[(U,f)]\cdot[(V,g)]=[(U\cap V,f|_{U\cap V}\,g|_{U\cap V})]$; that is, $R(X)=\varinjlim_{U}\mathcal O_X(U)$, the colimit of rings over the dense open subsets $U\subseteq X$ directed by reverse inclusion, with restriction maps. (Stacks defines a rational function as a rational map $X\dashrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}$, an equivalence class of morphisms $U\to\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}$ on dense opens under the same relation, and its ring structure through $\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}$ as a ring object; through the bijection $\operatorname{Mor}(U,\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z})=\mathcal O_X(U)$ of Stacks Example 01JH this is the ring above, as Stacks itself uses in the proof of Lemma 01RV. The DAG uses the description by sections given here, not the one by rational maps.)
